newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks higher, expected to firm slightly.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks higher, expected to firm slightly.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly higher on Tuesday and traders expected share prices to continue firming slightly thanks to stronger buying impulse.
They said higher trading volume supported a steady climb of Zagrebacka Banka shares, apparently on the back of its strong pre-tax earnings for the first six months.
"A rising trend exists. But it is not exactly steep, there is no reason for that," said Dubravko Zganec of brokerage Fima.
A trader at Metroholding brokerage cited Dalmatian hotel stocks as a good buy with good long-term growth potential as the country's tourist industry recovers.
She saw increasing demand among private investors giving a short term boost to shares in Podravka food-processing firm and confectioner Kras.

Both have been traded more actively in recent weeks amid media reports that they would draw investment by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and afterwards offer their shares on the international market, like Pliva.
Neither firms wanted to comment yet on the course of their negotiations with the EBRD and further plans.
* Four of eight traded issues rose, one fell and three remained unchanged.
* Most active Podravka was flat at 235 kuna with 3,188 shares sold.
* Zagrebacka Banka firmed 10 kuna to 740 on volume of 2,270 shares.
* The only loser hotelier Riviera, selling 86 shares, was down five kuna to 95.
* Pliva stable at 12,000 kuna on volume of 100 shares.
* Cable maker Elka rose 10 kuna to 135 with 114 units sold.
* Kras added five kuna to a new high of 315 on volume of 221 shares.
* Troubled Privredna Banka also up five kuna to 145 with 30 shares in a first deal since three weeks ago.
* Hotelier Suncani Hvar flat at 45 kuna on volume of 30.
* Total volume 6,039 shares, turnover down to 3.7 million kuna.
